mission_01: Well done! You have computed derivatives both analytically and numerically. The analytical derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x - 1 is f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 3, giving f'(2) = 7. The numerical approximation using central differences matches closely. The second derivative f''(2) = 8 tells us the function is concave up at x = 2. This ability to compute rates of change is the cornerstone of optimization — every gradient descent step relies on derivatives to find the direction of steepest descent.
